html:
The Yandruwandha are an Aboriginal Australian people of the lower Cooper Creek country, near Innamincka in far northeast South Australia. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Their land is dry, but the Cooper's long waterholes held fish and drew birds, and people ground the spores of the nardoo fern into flour. They are known to history through the Burke and Wills expedition of 1860 and 1861. On the way back from the Gulf, Robert O'Hara Burke and William Wills died of hunger on the Cooper in 1861, having failed to live on nardoo as the locals did. The third man, John King, survived because the Yandruwandha fed and sheltered him until a rescue party arrived. Neighbours on the map include the Dieri, the Yawarawarka and the Wadigali. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
